reason: A ratio fragment ('1/5-1/4 length of lemma', '2/3-3/4 as long as lemma'). The bearer is the part being described (palea, awn, callus, nerves). The lemma (PO_0009037) is only the second term of pattern 10, ratio to another part. This is the same decision as for 'fraction of leaf', 'fraction of tube' and 'times lemma'.

This is the umbo of a conifer seed-cone scale (Pinus: pyramidal, recurved, with a prickle). There is no class for the umbo, and no region in the patterns fits it: the umbo is terminal in some pines and dorsal on the apophysis in others, so 'apex of megasporophyll (PO_0009027)' would be wrong for half of them. 'fruit scale' and 'apophysis' were both rejected on 2026-11-14 as ambiguous.

Narrower: a freely ending veinlet that lies inside an areole. 'Included' places it in the areole and adds no new structure. The counts are per areole, so they are a count with leaf lamina areole (PO_0025392) as the container.
A quality adjective cut off from its noun ('irregular lobes', 'irregular rows', 'irregular pairs' of nerves). The counted parts are the lobes and nerves named after it.

Two different structures share this name. It can be the inflated basal chamber (utricle) of the Aristolochia perianth tube, or the lower chamber of an Arum spathe (spathe tube, FLOPO_0986047). The examples ('inside reddish', 'with alveolae', '1-2.5 cm') do not tell which, and the two need different targets.

Narrower: the strong lateral veins that arise at the base of the lamina in palmately or acrodromously veined leaves. This matches rule C272 ('basal vein' to leaf lamina vein). 'Major' and 'lateral' do not reliably map to a vein order: such veins are primary in some descriptions and secondary in others.

Narrower: in these floras (Urticaceae, Amaranthaceae) a glomerule is a dense, contracted cymose cluster of flowers. A male glomerule is a staminate partial inflorescence. Do not use the PO synonym 'glomerule' on compound capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030122); the 'per glomerule' review warned that it grounds wrongly.
These are the corolla plicae of Gentiana. The class exists, and 'apex' is a region the patterns express (plant organ apex of the plica). Acute, obtuse and long-fringed are qualities of that apex.
Narrower: a dot-like gland. 'gland' is a RELATED synonym of portion of secretory tissue (rule C265). 'Punctate' only describes the gland's shape and is not a separate structure.
A count of how the bristles are arranged ('bristles in 1 row per rib'). A row is a series, not a structure. This is the same decision as 'rows per locule' and 'areole row'.

Exact once 'small' is removed: 'small' is a size quality that was pulled into the name. The part is the gland (rule C265). The counts ('1 or 2 small glands on margin', 'at base') belong to the gland, with the organ named in the sentence as its container.

In Arisaema the throat is the mouth of the spathe tube, where the tube opens into the limb. The spathe tube class exists, so the throat can be expressed as its distal region rather than a new class. 'Throat' alone was rejected as generic, but here the organ is named.
The rim of the mouth of the spathe tube (Arisaema: 'throat margin recurved', 'auriculate', 'to 8 mm wide'). It is the margin region of the spathe tube, which the region patterns express.

target: trichome (PO_0000282, synonym scale) as part of stalk (PO_0025066), region margin
reason: These are the margins of the scales on a fern stipe (ciliate, with irregular processes). The scale is trichome (synonym scale), the stipe is stalk (rule C264), and the scale belongs to the stipe as a part of a qualified whole (pattern 12). The margin is a region the patterns express.

A ratio fragment ('1.5-2.0x as long as the tepals'). The tepal (PO_0009033) is the second term of pattern 10, ratio to another part, and not the bearer. This is the same decision as 'x perianth' and 'x calyx'.

A lobe of an organ that is not named, so it is a generic part. 'basal lobe' and 'lateral lobe' were both rejected for this reason on 2026-11-13. A lobe 'ca. 8 cm' could be a leaf lobe or an aroid blade lobe; without the organ it cannot be grounded.

A quality adjective (setose), not a part. The examples are pappus bristles ('pappus composed of a single whorl', 'of 10 or 11 bristles'). The structure there is the pappus (PO_0025393), and 'bristle' alone was rejected as generic.

target: region distal ('upper part') of the part being described, as the context word 'upper'
reason: The distal region of the organ named in the sentence (strigose, verrucose, smooth). config/flora_context_words.tsv already maps 'upper' and 'above' to region 'distal', so this should be another such context word, not a class. If the sentence names no organ, the statement should be dropped.
Related or narrower: a cluster of fruits borne together, either a whole infructescence or a partial one. PO lists 'fruit bunch' as a synonym. Length and diameter apply to the cluster as a whole.
A plural of a positioned part, built the same way as lateral leaflet (FLOPO_0996008) and median pinna (FLOPO_0996030) in config/flopo_positioned_parts.tsv. It can be added there as 'lateral pinna'.

A ratio fragment ('base ca. 1/2 as wide as nutlet'). The bearer is the part being described, and the nutlet's width is the second term of pattern 10. This is the same decision as 'fraction of leaf width'.
A fragment of a count at a position ('1-4 on basiscopic side'). No pattern covers the basiscopic position; see the 2026-11-14 rejection of 'basiscopic lobe'.
A fragment of a count at a position (pattern 14, '2-7 on each side of rachis'), with 'rachis' wrongly singularised. This is the same decision as 'per side of rachi' and 'on each side'.

Narrower: in tri- or more-pinnate fronds a pinnule is a pinna of a higher order, so its rachis is the rachis of a higher-order pinna. Grounding to pinna rachis is only right if FLOPO_0986065 is defined for pinnae of any order. If it is defined for primary pinnae only, reject this item instead of creating a new class (2 floras).

Exact in these floras: the nodes (joints) of the raceme rachis in grasses ('nodes pilose or glabrous'), where PO lists 'inflorescence rachis' as a synonym of inflorescence axis. In a fern flora the leaf rachis would be meant, so the rule should be limited to grass treatments.

Exact once 'raised' is removed: 'raised' is a surface quality, not a separate structure. The organ (bract, glume, fruit) is not named in the item, so the general vein target applies, as in rule C153 for 'nerve'.

label: spadix sterile zone
parent: is_a: same parent as its siblings spadix staminate zone (FLOPO_0986101) and spadix pistillate zone (FLOPO_0986105); part_of: spadix inflorescence (PO_0030120)
definition: A zone of the spadix that bears only sterile flowers (staminodes or pistillodes) or is naked, lying between or below the fertile zones. It is distinct from the terminal spadix appendix.
reason: A real structure that Araceae treatments describe all the time, with its own length, diameter and shape. FLOPO already has the staminate and pistillate zones and the appendix (FLOPO_0986049), so the sterile zone completes the set. It should be proposed to PO together with its sibling zones.

Narrower: a tooth that ends in a spine. 'Spinose' is a quality of the tooth. The teeth are on leaf lobes or on bracts and phyllaries, so the phyllome-level class covers both. Where the leaf is named, leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518) applies.
The base region of the staminode, which the region patterns express (plant organ base). Dilated, conic and curved, and its width, are qualities of that base.
A quality adjective (almost sessile) cut off from its noun ('12-18 pairs of subsessile pinnules'). The counted part is the pinnule (FLOPO_0985028).
